Can you do a complex gloss of the following text using the Leipzig glossing rules?  "Those who end up here have their souls stripped from them, leaving them as a conscious shell. They are left to wander an endless desert under a dying purple sun hanging over the horizon in perpetuality." Every quoted phrase must be followed by an unquoted explanation.assistant
response:
Here is the glossed text using the Leipzig glossing rules:

Those / who / end / up / here / have / their / souls / stripped / from / them / leaving / them / as / a / conscious / shell / They / are / left / to / wander / an / endless / desert / under / a / dying / purple / sun / hanging / over / the / horizon / in / perpetuity

Breakdown:

* Those: NOUN (singular, definite)
* who: PRONOUN (relative, singular)
* end: VERB (past tense, third person singular)
* up: ADVERB (indicating direction)
* here: ADVERB (indicating location)
* have: VERB (present tense, third person singular)
* their: ADJECTIVE (possessive, singular)
* souls: NOUN (plural, abstract)
* stripped: VERB (past participle, third person singular)
* from: PREPOSITION (indicating separation)
* them: PRONOUN (object, singular)
* leaving: VERB (present participle, third person singular)
* them: PRONOUN (object, singular)
* as: CONJUNCTION (subordinating, introducing a dependent clause)
* a: ARTICLE (indefinite, singular)
* conscious: ADJECTIVE (describing the noun)
* shell: NOUN (singular, concrete)
* They: PRONOUN (subject, plural)
* are: VERB (present tense, third person plural)
* left: VERB (past tense, third person singular)
* to: PREPOSITION (indicating direction)
* wander: VERB (present tense, third person singular)
* an: ARTICLE (indefinite, singular)
* endless: ADJECTIVE (describing the noun)
* desert: NOUN (singular, concrete)
* under: PREPOSITION (indicating location)
* a: ARTICLE (indefinite, singular)
* dying: ADJECTIVE (describing the noun)
* purple: ADJECTIVE (describing the noun)
* sun: NOUN (singular, concrete)
* hanging: VERB (present participle, third person singular)
* over: PREPOSITION (indicating location)
* the: ARTICLE (definite, singular)
* horizon: NOUN (singular, concrete)
* in: PREPOSITION (indicating location)
* perpetuity: NOUN (singular, abstract)

Note: The Leipzig glossing rules are a set of conventions for representing the grammatical structure of a sentence in a concise and standardized way. They are commonly used in linguistic analysis and are particularly useful for representing the grammatical structure of languages that do not have a simple verb-subject-object word order.
